newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal ruling party wins two seats in by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Nepal ruling party wins two seats in by-elections.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba on Monday won two of five by-elections held on Friday but was frustrated in his efforts to become the largest political force, officials said.

The Himalayan kingdom's Election Commission said M. Aftab Alam of Deuba's Nepali Congress party won the Rautahat Two parliamentary seat, taking the final tally for his party to 87 in the 205-member House of Representatives.
Earlier on Monday, Keshab Bahadur Chand, also from the Nepali Congress, won Baitadi One constituency in Nepal's far west.
"The outcome is the reflection of the organisational weaknesses and non-performance of the government," said Shushil Koirala, General Secretary of Deuba's Nepali Congress.
The by-elections were the first popular vote since Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party formed a fractious coalition government in September 1995.
The opposition Communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party's three victories secured its position as the single largest party in the hung parliament.
With its fresh gains, the UML has increased its position to 90 seats from 87 in the 205-member House of Representatives but still lacks the required majority to force Deuba out.
An election official told Reuters that the result of the fifth by-election in Rautahat Two parliamentary seat was expected to be announced later on Monday.
Deuba survived a no-confidence vote last month but has promised to call a confidence vote when parliament convenes next month.
Analysts said the outcome of the by-elections was crucial for Deuba's fractured three-party coalition which technically commands a majority but is immobilised by fissures among its constituents.
The UML has already demanded Deuba's resignation saying that his government has lost the support of the people.
"The prime minister should immediately resign," UML's General Secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal told Reuters on Sunday.
Parliamentary elections are not scheduled until 1999 in the kingdom.
